description: Figure 9 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the effect of context masking perturbations on model performance, categorized by linguistic tag (case, gender, tag, number, tense) and model variant. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is scaled from 0 to 20, representing the percentage reduction (or improvement, if negative) in probing accuracy relative to the unperturbed baseline, as defined by Equation (1) in the text. The horizontal axis lists five linguistic categories: “case,” “gender,” “tag,” “number,” and “tense.” For each category, six bars are grouped together, corresponding to six model configurations: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. Error bars extending vertically from each bar represent the standard deviation of the effect measurement. The “case” category shows the largest effects across most models, particularly for mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂, which reach approximately 12–13% effect. In contrast, “tense” shows minimal effects, mostly near zero or slightly negative, indicating little to no degradation (or even slight improvement) in accuracy. The “gender” and “tag” categories show moderate effects, generally between 0 and 5%, while “number” shows small effects, mostly under 3%. The chart visually demonstrates that context masking perturbations have the most pronounced impact on case-related tasks and the least on tense-related tasks across the evaluated models.
